newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs sell 100,000 tonnes wheat to Uzbekistan.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs sell 100,000 tonnes wheat to Uzbekistan.

text.p: An official at Kazakhstan's agriculture ministry said on Monday the ex-Soviet republic had sold 100,000 tonnes of wheat from state reserves to grain hungry neighbour Uzbekistan last week.

"Kazakhstan signed a contract with Uzbekistan for 100,000 tonnes of wheat," Alexander Korablin, spokesman for the agriculture ministry, told Reuters by telephone. "If we fulfil the terms of the contract on time, Uzbekistan will buy another 100,000 tonnes," he said.
Korablin was unable to give any more details on the deal while officials from Kazakhstan's state food corporation, which oversaw the transaction, were not immediately available for comment.
Grain sources in secretive Uzbekistan said in February that the republic was in the market for around 1-1.2 million tonnes of food wheat this year.
The mostly desert country of Uzbekistan, the world's second largest cotton exporter, is short of grain to feed its 23 million people who rely increasingly on bread as a cheap source of food.
Uzbekistan's annual grain demand is about 3.5-4 million tonnes, but last year's harvest was just 2.7 million tonnes, way below a 4.5 million tonne state target.
